An equation (or inequality) involving a complex number z=x+yi can be an efficient way to represent a line, curve or area in x - y space. Writing in terms of x and y can help to sketch the locus. A reminder of some relationships are given in table 1. Consider the expression \left|z-w\right| which is equivalent to \sqrt{{(x-a)}^{2}+{(y-b)}^{2}} , and so can describe loci associated with the circle with centre at w=(a,b) . When this is an inequality, the locus is all the points inside or outside the circle (blue and green). When it is an equality the locus contains all the points on the circle (red). For example, consider the locus given by 2<\left|z\right|\leq 5 It includes all points that are outside the circle {x}^{2}+{y}^{2}=4 and inside or on the circle {x}^{2}+{y}^{2}=25 . Recap Key points from section 5.5 •​Equations and inequalities using complex numbers can be an efficient way to represent sets of points (loci) in x - y space. •​These could be points, lines, or areas depending on the form of the expression, but the resulting expression should not contain i . •​Writing the expression in terms of x and y can help to find the curves •​Some simple examples are the equation of a circle \left|z-w\right|=R and straight line \operatorname{Im}\left(z\right)=mRe\left(z+c\right) (where m is real) Previous page
